Leaf blowers: blowing, collecting and mulching are separate jobs

Check which modes the complete machine supports

A blower-only tool moves leaves; a blower-vac also needs a collection arrangement. Confirm the bag, tubes and conversion steps included in a combined model. Wet leaves and gravel paths create different limitations, so read the exact manual rather than treating maximum air speed as a cleaning-performance test. A mulching ratio is not a guarantee for every type or condition of garden debris.

Plan power, weight and disposal

A cordless tool needs its battery, charger and runtime conditions checked. A mains machine needs safe cable reach and the manufacturer's outdoor electrical guidance; a petrol model has fuel, servicing and storage requirements. Compare carrying weight with the collection bag filling, not only the empty tool. Decide where collected leaves will go before paying for a vacuum mode you may not use.

Although we have not physically tested every item featured, our methodology is designed to help consumers make informed and confident purchasing decisions. Where performance, safety or durability are especially important, we also encourage checking independent reviews of the exact model.
